title: Hook
text: Why are galaxies not flying apart into total chaos right now? According to the established laws of physics, they should be.
nxt: The story of how we found out begins with a simple question about speed.

title: Planet Speeds
text: In our solar system, distant planets drift lazily while inner worlds race around the Sun.
nxt: Mercury speeds along at roughly forty-seven kilometers per second, while distant Neptune plods along at less than six.

title: What Astronomers Expected
text: Astronomers expected the same rule in galaxies.
nxt: According to the established laws of physics, stars near the outer rim of a galaxy should move much slower than stars near the crowded center.

title: Torn Apart
text: These stars were moving so rapidly that the visible gravity of the galaxy could not possibly hold them.
nxt: By all ordinary logic, these swirling galaxies should have torn themselves apart and flung their stars into the dark void long ago.

title: The Invisible Halo
text: Scientists suspect that an immense, invisible halo of mysterious mass surrounds each galaxy, providing the extra gravitational glue needed to hold everything together.
nxt: Because this substance emits no light, absorbs no light, and reflects no light, we simply call it dark matter.

title: Bending Light
text: Other evidence agrees. Massive clusters of galaxies stretch the light of galaxies far behind them into glowing arcs, and the bending is stronger than the visible matter can explain.
nxt: The extra mass is clearly there. It simply does not shine.

title: Phantom Matter
text: Dark matter is not made of protons, neutrons, or electrons.
nxt: If a cloud of it passed through your living room right now, you would not see it, hear it, or feel it.
